transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Anita Rao (BlueHarbor Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Platform Eng), Eli Turner (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey all, thanks for joining, I think we've got most folks on. This is Maya from Redwood, AE, and Liam our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Anita: Good, thanks. We're curious to understand Dedicated — we've been evaluating hosted but need isolation for PCI card tokenization flows.
[00:18] Liam: Great, thanks Anita. We'll focus on reserved GPU pools, isolation, and how burst works. Quick intro: Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity that sits in a customer-specific pool, can be VPC peered or private deployments, and you can configure autoscaling + burst policies.
[00:35] Carlos: When you say "burst" — do you mean we get extra GPUs on demand? We have big spikes during checkout windows.
[00:42] Liam: Two pieces — we do reserved baseline, then we have an optional burst tier that can draw from a shared pool or from cloud spot capacity, depending on whether you want strict isolation. For PCI, most customers prefer reserved baseline plus scheduled burst windows, or a hybrid where burst is limited to non-PCI endpoints.
[00:58] Eli: What about SLAs for latency under burst? If a rush happens, we can't have 500ms spikes.
[01:05] Maya: We offer latency SLOs for Dedicated — usually 99th percentile targets based on model and sequence length. For strict enterprise SLAs we can contract specific p99s. We'll need to size GPUs by tokens/s and concurrency.
[01:18] Anita: Our current inference is on k8s with Triton and some custom batching. We do around 120 QPS at peak, typical completion 400-600 tokens, and p90 latency target of 200-250ms.
[01:30] Liam: Good — that helps. For 120 QPS and 400 tokens, we typically recommend a mix of A100/RTX-class instances depending on model. Also quantization and KV cache will affect memory — do you use context reuse?
[01:44] Carlos: Yes, we reuse prompts heavily — there's a lot of prefix caching. We also do reranking offline.
[01:50] Liam: OK KV cache (sometimes transcribed as "KV cash" in notes) helps a lot, reduces compute for repeated sequences. We'll send a sizing exercise but expect you'll need X reserved GPUs for baseline, plus Y for burst depending on acceptable p99.
[02:05] Anita: Are there options for private control plane? Our security team wants control plane inside our VPC.
[02:10] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private offers a private control plane with VPC peering or on-prem options. You can run the control plane in your VPC and data stays in your network. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[02:22] Eli: KMS — do you integrate with AWS KMS/HSM? We use HSM for key crypto.
[02:27] Liam: We integrate with AWS KMS and can support HSM workflows; keys never leave your keyspace. We also provide audit logs and per-request lineage.
[02:35] Carlos: Audit logs retention — we have to keep logs for 1 year for PCI compliance. Do you support long retention or do we need to pull them?
[02:42] Maya: We have an add-on for extended log retention, yes. We'll include that in the pricing doc.
[02:48] Anita: How about model variants? We sometimes need a smaller model for low-cost fallbacks.
[02:53] Liam: Smart routing supports tiered routing by cost/latency; can fallback to quantized or smaller model if baseline is saturated. That is part of the Dedicated runtime.
[03:02] Eli: Any live customers using private Dedicated for payments?
[03:05] Maya: We have a couple of fintechs in beta; I can anonymize references.
[03:09] Carlos: What's the typical lead time for provisioning reserved GPUs?
[03:13] Liam: Usually 2-4 weeks from contract to provisioning, quicker if we have cloud infra details and a pilot config. For private, add time for network setup.
[03:24] Anita: On benchmarking — we'd like to run our prompt set. Do you provide a benchmark harness?
[03:28] Liam: Yes, we'll send a benchmark script that runs your prompts, does concurrency sweeps, and reports latency/cost. We'll run it on a 48-hour pilot reserved cluster.
[03:36] Maya: Next steps we'd propose: send pricing + sizing options, share benchmark script, customer supplies prompts and expected SLOs, schedule pilot the week of 2026-03-30.
[03:46] Anita: Sounds good. A couple of nitty-gritty questions — SSO/SAML for console access, RBAC?
[03:51] Maya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls.
[03:57] Carlos: Data residency — we operate in us-east-1 only, need all data to remain in region.
[04:02] Liam: We can pin regions for Dedicated and Private; we'll note that in the sizing doc.
[04:08] Eli: Pricing model — is Dedicated flat monthly or usage based on GPU hours?
[04:12] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) plus potential overage/burst billing; hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll include T-shirt sizing options and baseline vs burst cost tradeoffs.
[04:22] Anita: Any potential gotchas? We've heard about tokenization differences across vendor runtimes.
[04:26] Liam: Right — tokenizer mismatches can affect token counts and cost. We'll validate tokenization and provide a mapping. Also for quantized models, you might see output differences; we'll run quality checks as part of the benchmark.
[04:40] Carlos: On security docs — can you share SOC2, penetration test results, and a network diagram?
[04:44] Maya: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II and the latest pentest summary; network diagram included.
[04:49] Anita: For the pilot, what metrics should we look at?
[04:52] Liam: Latency (p50/p90/p99), tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and any quality regressions vs your baseline. We'll provide dashboards.
[05:02] Eli: If the pilot looks good, what's the contract cadence?
[05:05] Maya: Typically we move to a reserved contract for Dedicated after pilot, with options for monthly or annual commitments and SLAs.
[05:12] Anita: A random question — do you do autoscaling on GPUs or just queueing?
[05:16] Liam: Autoscaling occurs at the pool level; we can scale node counts and redistribute model shards, but scaling has coordination time — that's why burst pools are useful for fast capacity.
[05:27] Carlos: Any limitations around model size? We run some 70B models taking up a lot of GPU memory.
[05:31] Liam: We support sharded execution and recommend specific instance classes for 70B. We'll call out model-specific kernel and compilation notes.
[05:38] Anita: Okay — timeline wise we need an internal security review by 2026-03-25, so if we can get docs and pricing by 3/20 that's ideal.
[05:45] Maya: Noted. We'll target 3/20 for docs and pricing.
[05:49] Carlos: Can we get a sample SLA language for p99?
[05:52] Maya: Yes, we'll attach sample SLA clauses.
[05:54] Eli: One last ops question — does Redwood provide out-of-band support during the pilot?
[05:58] Liam: Yes, dedicated onboarding and 24/7 support options for pilots and customers on Dedicated.
[06:03] Anita: Great. I think that's it. Thanks everyone.
[06:06] Maya: Thanks — recap: Maya sends pricing + dedicated options and SOC2/pentest, Liam sends benchmark script and infra checklist, Anita/Carlos send prompts and SLOs. Schedule pilot for week of 3/30.
[06:18] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings, e.g., "KV cache" shown as "KV cash" in one section; speaker labels sometimes simplified. References to Redwood product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood API.
